doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Cincinnati bands, race and the road to college
title: Segregated audiences and the white slummers
summary: The band played to black audiences only, with a few white 'slummers' or music lovers attending.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In these places, were you playing for black folks, white folks, mixed audiences?
We played for black folks. There were no mixed audiences in those days. You either played for all black audiences or all white audiences.
Would there be some white people at the black thing but no black people at the white thing?
Exactly, yeah. Some white, only a smattering.
Were they typically musicians or more hip people? Who were the whites who ventured into the black world to hear this music?

A lot of them were so-called slummers. You know, “Let’s go slumming tonight. Let’s go see what’s happening,” and so forth. Not particularly hip people but people who -- they may have had black friends who brought them to the affairs, or they may have been people who actually had an appreciation for music and who didn’t know where else they would be able to hear this band, so they would come to this black dance.
